notes: Body independently checked. The selector 0x13 tests are 1, 3, 4, and 5 (the proposal omitted 4); a matching path calls the record lookup, and when it returns a record the u16 field at +0x32 gates the result. It then checks selector 0x14 against 2 and 3. Corrected to avoid asserting a simpler OR than the control flow supports. Call sites inspected at main_0058.c:21080,21093 and main_0094.c:29838.

Body and callers checked. An inactive object byte at +0x428 returns -2. Otherwise, a nonnull second argument uses its nested provider at +8 and selector 0x16, converts the float to signed integer and adds one; a null nested provider returns the third argument clamped below at -2. The name is a conservative description of this behavior. Call sites inspected at main_0111.c:50129 and main_0112.c:8118,26449.

Body and caller checked. The proposal is incomplete: the body can return true when selector 0x13 is 4 and selector 0x18 is 1; it also returns true when selector 0x13 is not 4 and selector 0x18 is neither 0 nor 4. All other observed branches return false. The broader name avoids claiming the predicate is limited to selector 0x13 equal to 4. Caller inspected at main_0006.c:34942.

Body and callers checked. The proposal says “clamped,” but this is a category mapping: for the active object it gets selector 0x16 from the nested provider (or uses the third argument when that provider is absent), then returns 2 above 20, 1 above 10, 3 above 4, or 0 otherwise; inactive object returns -2. The revised name describes the classification and threshold inputs without implying clamping. Call sites inspected at main_0112.c:2958,7330.

Body and callers checked. The body selects metric 0x11 when the third argument low bit is set, otherwise 0x1c; it evaluates the indexed metric at index zero and maps the float through fixed thresholds to integers 7 through 0. Calling the result a “grade” is not established by the body or callers, so the corrected name sticks to the visible bucket mapping. Call sites inspected at main_0113.c:3992,11604,11609.
